root_cause: get_authorization_scheme_param() splits the Authorization header with str.partition(" ") and returns the remainder verbatim, so extra spaces between scheme and token ("Bearer   xxx") or trailing whitespace ("Bearer xxx ") stay in the credentials string, violating RFC 6750 where spaces are only separators.
best_solution: In fastapi/security/utils.py, change `return scheme, param` to `return scheme, param.strip()`. Every security scheme (HTTPBase, HTTPBearer, OAuth2 bearer variants) routes through this one helper, so stripping the post-partition remainder fixes leading multi-space and trailing whitespace for all of them at once; scheme stays unchanged and empty/missing headers still return ("", "").
hidden_test_demands: tests/test_security_http_base.py::test_security_http_base_with_whitespaces sends 'Authorization: Other  foobar ' and expects 200 with {"scheme": "Other", "credentials": "foobar"}; tests/test_security_oauth2_authorization_code_bearer.py::test_token_with_whitespaces sends 'Bearer  testtoken ' and expects {"token": "testtoken"}. Both require stripping both leading (double space) and trailing whitespace from the credential.
locating_signals: Statement names the function get_authorization_scheme_param() and the file fastapi/security/utils.py and gives the exact one-line diff `return scheme, param.strip()`. Keywords: Authorization header, credentials, HTTPBearer.
our_outcome_summary: Solved by all four configs (v4/v6/v7/v8 kaggle_env_pass true). All four agent patches are byte-identical to the gold patch (404 chars), in 43-55 s and 14-20 tool calls on the pod.
generalizable_lesson: When the problem statement is a PR description that already contains the code change (a 'Solution' snippet plus a 'Changes' bullet naming function and file), apply exactly that edit in the named shared helper rather than patching individual callers; fixing the single chokepoint makes every caller's hidden tests pass, and extra caller-level changes only add risk.
acceptable_alternatives: Equivalent: return scheme, param.lstrip().rstrip(), or use authorization_header_value.split(None, 1) then strip. Stripping only leading spaces would fail both hidden tests because they include a trailing space. Changing the scheme to be case-normalized or stripping inside each security class would be unnecessary.
